cohort: 886 low-risk women who gave birth in either the hands-and-knees position (n=446) or the supine position (n=440) in 11 hospitals in China
finding: Women who delivered in the hands-and-knees position had lower rates of episiotomy and second-degree perineum laceration, higher rates of intact perineum and first-degree perineum laceration, and a longer duration of second stage of labor compared to those who delivered in the supine position.
mod_finding: The hands-and-knees delivery position was associated with lower rates of episiotomy and second-degree perineum laceration.
birth_weight: Birth weight was used as a covariate in the analysis
